newsitem.title: USA: Two U.S. senators want fourth Bosnia force.
newsitem.headline: Two U.S. senators want fourth Bosnia force.

text.p: Two U.S. senators said on Friday that a new NATO peacekeeping force will be needed in Bosnia when the present one leaves in 18 months, but it should be led by Europeans and include no U.S. combat troops.

Sen. Carl Levin of Michigan, senior Democrat on the Senate Armed Services Committee, and Sen. Jack Reed, Democrat of Rhode Island, said planning should begin immediately for what would be the fourth peacekeeping force in Bosnia.

"The hatreds are so deep, so longstanding that I just don't see this simmering down in the next 18 months to a point where there will be no need for further armed force," Levin said at a news conference.
He said the new force will be needed because predominantly Serb war criminals are unlikely to be arrested, 2.5 million refugees resettled and new civilian government agencies set up in 18 months.
But Levin and Reed, who recently returned from a trip to Bosnia and the Balkans, said the United States should provide only logistical and possibly air support for the new force.
They said the new force should be led by a new European Security Defence group in NATO, formed for Europeans to take a bigger role in the alliance.
The first peacekeeping force in Bosnia was led by the United Nations. A NATO peacekeeping force took over last year and a smaller NATO force is there now.
